City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 2, 2020  2
   C. PURCHASE OF AERIAL TREE TRIMMING TRUCK

  The Public Works Department is responsible for the regular maintenance of
  the City’s urban forest consisting of approximately 8,000 residential street and
  park trees. Our in-house crew supplements the outside tree-trimming
  contract by responding to regular residential customer service requests, tree
  pruning, removal of dead or diseased trees and emergency hazardous branch
  and tree removals, which has been saving the City money by not having to
  utilize an outside contract that can be significantly more expensive. This new
  aerial tree trimming truck will have a 55-foot ability to reach the top of the
  tree canopies which would replace the existing 20-year-old truck that requires
  more maintenance and longer periods of non-operation due to breakdowns.
  The cost of the aerial truck is $174,001.47.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Waive formal bidding and authorize the cooperative purchase with Altec
  Industries, Incorporated; and
  2. Approve the reallocation of $40,000 Measure R Funds in account 124-800-
  58-99-225 approved in the FY 19-20 Budget for a changeable message
  sign trailer, to be used towards the purchase of the aerial truck in account
  124-800-58-99-204; and
  3. Approve the reallocation of $14,001.47 from Gas Tax funds in account 124-
  800-41-96-513 approved in the FY 19-20 Budget for wayfinding signs, to
  be used towards the purchase of the aerial truck in account 124-800-41-
  99-767; and
  4. Approve the purchase of the Altec Model L-R7-52RM articulating aerial
  truck using account 124-800-58-99-204 for $160,000 (Measure R Funds)
  and account 124-800-41-99-767 for $14,001.47 (Gas Tax Fund); and
  5. Authorize the issuance of a Purchase Order to Altec Industries,
  Incorporated for an articulating aerial truck for $174,001.74 that includes
  taxes, delivery, Department of Motor Vehicles registration and the
  standard Altec Industries, Incorporated warranty.

  D. REVISED AMENDMENT TO TICKETMASTER AGREEMENT

  In February 2020, staff brought a report to the City Council requesting that
  the Council ratify the original Ticketmaster Agreement and approve an
  Amendment to the User Agreement. The City Council raised several questions
  about the Amended Agreement and agreed that they would like to see a

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 2, 2020  3
   revised Amendment which would address the issues raised. The Mission
  Playhouse receives a revenue of $2.00 per ticket purchased over the phone,
  online or in person. There are no fees or payments made by the Mission
  Playhouse and the City of San Gabriel as it pertains to the User Agreement.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Ratify the Ticketmaster User Agreement from December 2016; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve the revised Amendment to the
  User Agreement which extends services for an additional three (3) years
  and includes amendments to the fee structure.

  E. ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING MISSION PLAYHOUSE
  GRANT WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY FIFTH SUPERVISORIAL DISTRICT

  The City of San Gabriel was awarded funding for the Mission Playhouse
  through a Proposition A Grant from Los Angeles County 5th Supervisorial
  District. The grant, totaling $60,000, will fund the purchase of an upgraded
  audio mixing console and an updated lighting/dimming system, both of
  which are in need of replacement. The equipment purchase will be included
  as a special project in Fiscal Year 2020-21.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Resolution No. 20-28, including the required Youth Employment
  Plan; and
  2. Authorize staff to move forward with the grant application for project
  funds and enter into an agreement with Los Angeles County Regional Park
  and Open Space District.

  F. HINDERLITER, DE LLAMAS & ASSOCIATES,  LIMITED  LIABILITY
  COMPANY SALES TAX REVIEW AGREEMENT

  On March 3, 2020, the voters of the San Gabriel elected to enact a ¾ cent
  transaction and use tax in the City. As part of the normal course of business
  and in the interest of prudency, the City annually contracts with Hinderliter,
  de Llamas & Associates, LLC (HDL) for the review and projection of its Sales
  Tax (Bradley-Burns 1% portion). With this additional sales tax now added, the

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 2, 2020  4
   City wishes to also have this portion reviewed by HDL. Furthermore, the
  overseeing State agency of this implementation (the California Department
  of Tax and Fee Administration (CAFTFA), is requiring a formal contract for any
  parties reviewing this new transaction tax.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. 20-26
  approving a five-year agreement with HDL to review and provide projections
  on the City’s new transaction tax.

5.  PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTIONS APPROVING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-21
  OPERATING BUDGET AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM AND
  ESTABLISHING THE 2020-21 APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT

  The report provides a summary of the Proposed Budget and Capital
  Improvement Plan (CIP) for Fiscal Year 2020-21. The operating budget is
  balanced, with revenues totaling $69,483,901 and expenditures totaling
  $68,273,699. The CIP totals $6,191,594, providing new/additional funding for
  16 projects.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council conduct a public hearing on the 2020-
  21 Operating and Capital Improvement Program Budgets and after receiving
  comments and testimony adopt the following resolutions:

  1. Resolution No. 20-29 Adopting the City of San Gabriel FY 2020-21
  Operating Budget; and
  2. Resolution No. 20-24 Approving the City of San Gabriel 2020-21 to 2024-
  25 Five-Year Capital Improvement Program and Adopting the 2020-21
  Capital Improvement Program Budget; and
  3. Resolution No. 20-27 Establishing the City of San Gabriel’s Appropriation
  Limit for the FY 2020-21.

6.  NEW BUSINESS

  A. ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING NON-EXCLUSIVE
  TOWING SERVICE FRANCHISES

 City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 2, 2020  5
   The City of San Gabriel currently operates its police-initiated tow service
  through an informal agreement, rather than the industry standard franchise
  agreement. While the informal agreement the City used in the past has been
  satisfactory, the benefits of a towing service franchise agreement include a
  reduction in City liability and exposure, better control of the service provided
  to the public, and a method of cost recovery for City administrative costs.
  These agreements ensure appropriate authorities and responsibilities are
  identified for the security of vehicles and other property in addition to
  administration of police-related vehicle impounds, storage, and other tow-
  related operations. Overall, a franchise agreement would ultimately ensure
  the quality and professionalism of the towing service representing the City.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Introduce, for first reading by title only, proposed Ordinance No. 664 for
  adoption into the City of San Gabriel Municipal Code, establishing non-
  exclusive towing services franchises and authorizing entrance into towing
  agreements with qualified tow-service providers; and
  2. Waive further reading of Ordinance No. 664 and schedule the second
  reading and adoption of the Ordinance.

  B. 2019 GENERAL PLAN IMPLEMENTATION ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT:
  JANUARY 2019 – DECEMBER 2019

  As required by Government Code Section 65400(a)(2), the Planning Division
  is required to provide an annual report each April to the City Council, and the
  State Governor’s Office of Planning and Research (OPR) regarding the status
  of the General Plan and its implementation progress. The Planning
  Commission reviewed the report at their May 11, 2020 meeting, affirmed the
  information in the report and recommended it be forwarded to the City
  Council.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council affirm the information contained in
  the General Plan Implementation Report for the period January 2019 to
  December 2019 and direct staff to send the documents to the State
  Governor’s Office of Planning and Research.

 7. PUBLIC COMMENT

MINUTES OF JUNE 2, 2020
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
6:38 p.m. on Tuesday, June 2, 2020, with all Council Members and staff participating by
teleconference.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

City Attorney Lemieux announced that for the Special Meeting held at 5:30 P.M. this
evening, there was no reportable action.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Liao.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux,  Assistant  City  Manager/Community
  Development Director Arminé Chaparyan, Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Rebecca
  Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk
  Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Interim Finance Director Kenneth Louie, and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

Mayor Menchaca provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
submit comments.
1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  City Attorney Lemieux requested that the City Council consider adding an item
  entitled, “Justice for George Floyd Briefing,” to the agenda as a Presentation item,
  which would require a two-thirds affirmative vote, with findings that the need to take
  action came to the attention of the City subsequent to the posting of the agenda and
  with the need to take action prior to the next scheduled meeting.

  A motion was made by Council Member Pu, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to approve
  the agenda order as amended, with the aforementioned findings.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA

   NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. PROCLAMATION CONGRATULATING SAN GABRIEL GRADUATES

  Presentation was made by Mayor Menchaca.

  B. JUSTICE FOR GEORGE FLOYD BRIEFING

  Presentations were made by Police Chief Harris and Fire Chief Wallace.

  C. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  Mayor Menchaca announced that this will be an ongoing presentation on the
  Agenda until the COVID-19 epidemic ends to keep the public informed directly
  from the City’s first responders and staff.

  Presentations were made by Fire Chief Wallace, Police Chief Harris, and City
  Manager Lazzaretto.

3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Donna Lee, of AskDonna1-2-3- Wellness, requested that funding for the San Gabriel
  Chamber of Commerce be continued.

4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Council Member Harrington pulled item 4D and Council Member Pu pulled item 4C
  for separate discussion.

  Regarding item 4D, Council Member Harrington expressed concerns about the high
  charges and fees to be paid to Ticketmaster and his disagreement with the City
  indemnifying Ticketmaster.

  In response to questions from Vice Mayor Liao, Community Services/Interim Mission
  Playhouse Director Perez clarified that there is no termination cost for the proposed
  three-year agreement.

  Regarding item 4C, discussion included the need for purchasing a new tree-trimming
  truck versus a changeable message sign; details on the current heavy usage; repair
  frequency and duration, and approaching emissions expiration date for the existing
  tree-trimming truck; cleaner emissions, cost-savings, and pricing for a new truck;
  usage for changeable message signs; new vehicle warranty; emissions rules; funding
  sources for the new vehicle; and alternate-fuel vehicle pros and cons.

  A motion was made by Council Member Harrington, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to
  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A – 4C and 4E – 4F as presented.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4A – 4C and 4E – 4F as presented by a vote of
  5-0 as follows:
  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 6  June 2, 2020
   ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following items as presented:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of May 12, 2020, 5:30 P.M.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of May 19, 2020
  3. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of May 19, 2020

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved the May 7, 2020, and May 14, 2020 Registers of

  C. PURCHASE OF AERIAL TREE-TRIMMING TRUCK

  The City Council:

  1. Waived formal bidding and authorized the cooperative purchase with Altec
  Industries, Incorporated; and
  2. Approved the reallocation of $40,000 Measure R Funds in account 124-800-58-
  99-225 approved in the FY 19-20 Budget for a changeable message sign trailer,
  to be used towards the purchase of the aerial truck in account 124-800-58-99-
  204; and
  3. Approved the reallocation of $14,001.47 from Gas Tax funds in account 124-
  800-41-96-513 approved in the FY 19-20 Budget for wayfinding signs, to be
  used towards the purchase of the aerial truck in account 124-800-41-99-767;
  and
  4. Approved the purchase of the Altec Model L-R7-52RM articulating aerial truck
  using account 124-800-58-99-204 for $160,000 (Measure R Funds) and account
  124-800-41-99-767 for $14,001.47 (Gas Tax Fund); and
  5. Authorized the issuance of a Purchase Order to Altec Industries, Incorporated
  for an articulating aerial truck for $174,001.74 that includes taxes, delivery,
  Department of Motor Vehicles registration and the standard Altec Industries,
  Incorporated warranty.

  D. REVISED AMENDMENT TO TICKETMASTER AGREEMENT

  This item was not approved.

  E. ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING MISSION PLAYHOUSE
  GRANT WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY FIFTH SUPERVISORIAL DISTRICT

  The City Council:

  1. Adopted Resolution No. 20-28, including the required Youth Employment
  Plan; and
  2. Authorized staff to move forward with the grant application for project funds
  and enter into an agreement with Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open
  Space District.

  F. HINDERLITER, DE LLAMAS & ASSOCIATES, LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY
  SALES TAX REVIEW AGREEMENT
CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 6  June 2, 2020
   The City Council adopted Resolution No. 20-26 approving a five-year agreement
  with HDL to review and provide projections on the City’s new transaction tax.
5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTIONS APPROVING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-21
  OPERATING BUDGET AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM AND
  ESTABLISHING THE 2020-21 APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT

  The staff presentation was made by Management Specialist Julia James.

  Mayor Menchaca opened the public hearing.

  The following provided comments in favor of including funding for the San Gabriel
  Chamber of Commerce in the Fiscal Year (FY) 2020-21 Budget: Alexis Salamanca,
  resident, Eraxtyle Design owner; Gilda Moshir, PHP Agency; Regina Bory, Re/Max
  Olympic; Devlin Chung; Camelia Vera, Coldwell Banker George Realty; and Paul
  Cheng, PPRClaw, APC.

  The following provided comments in opposition to including funding for the San
  Gabriel Chamber of Commerce in the FY 2020-21 Budget: Cheri Cabot; and Sean
  McMorris, resident.

  The following provided comments in support of increasing funding for Community
  Services, Disaster Relief and Community outreach programs: Isela Salazar.

  Mayor Menchaca closed the public hearing.

  Discussion included the budget as a planning document requiring periodic
  adjustments; the uncertainty of revenues given COVID-19 effects; cuts already
  made to protect staffing levels in order to maintain services to the community; a
  desire to have contracts for any payment to outside entities; the need to trade-off
  one piece of needed equipment for another due to limited funds; the need for
  flexibility during the fiscal year while still having transparency and accountability;
  animal control services costs; consultant versus in-house facilitation for a new
  strategic plan and timing for a new plan; reducing the City Council travel and
  conference budget and getting Council pre-approval for attendance; the value of
  membership in various outside regional organizations; the amount proposed for
  Historic Preservation ordinance implementation; appreciation for staff having
  contingencies in case of revenue projection shortfalls; desire for monthly budget
  updates; having another budget study session before making final decisions; and
  starting the budget process earlier next year.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, with an amendment by Council Member
  Pu, to continue this item to meetings on June 9, 2020, and June 16, 2020.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING NON-EXCLUSIVE TOWING
  SERVICE FRANCHISES
CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  June 2, 2020
   The staff report was presented by Police Chief Harris.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included a request for future updates and criteria for choosing

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Mayor Menchaca, to:

  1. Introduce, for first reading by title only, Ordinance No. 664 establishing non-
  exclusive towing services franchises and authorizing entrance into towing
  agreements with qualified tow-service providers; and
  2. Waive further reading of Ordinance No. 664 and schedule the second reading

  Motion approved New Business Item 6A as presented by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  B. 2019 GENERAL PLAN IMPLEMENTATION ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT:
  JANUARY 2019 – DECEMBER 2019

  The staff report was presented by Management Specialist Mark Gallatin.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included the status of an upcoming affordable housing project;
